# Customer Escalations Agent — Overview

**Template.** These runbooks and agents are examples. They cover the full path to a production build and must be modified to meet each customer's specific requirements. The customer or their partner connects them to their own systems, identity, data and governance in their environment.

Resolve escalations with context, not guesswork

Bring fictional case history, knowledge guidance, routing rules, and quality signals into one reviewable brief so service teams can respond consistently without letting the agent touch a customer record.

**Why try it:** The demo lets a back-office agent ask a natural question and receive a source-backed, reviewable answer with the approval boundary visible in the response.

## Problem Statement

Back-office teams lose time reconciling CRM, knowledge, policy, and SLA context while high-risk cases wait and avoidable handoff errors compound.

## Solution Summary

Copilot Studio provides the conversation layer; Dynamics 365 Customer Service, SharePoint knowledge, Teams, and Outlook can supply governed production context after connection review.

**Blueprint role:** Creates a governed escalation-intelligence layer between fragmented service evidence and authorized human response.

**Capabilities:** Inquiry triage brief; Knowledge evidence search; Escalation routing review; Quality and satisfaction review. See [responsibilities and trust boundaries](2.Architecture.md).

## Business Outcomes

- Speeds evidence gathering for complex escalations.
- Improves consistency of knowledge and routing review.
- Gives quality teams a shared view of recurring service signals.

Claims are qualitative; synthetic demo figures are not customer results or performance commitments. See the [claims policy](../../solutions/README.md#claims-policy).

## Target Users

| Role | Need |
| --- | --- |
| Back-Office Agent | Get an inherited-escalation brief and the matching approved article before responding; the reply stays with the agent. |
| Escalation Manager | See which queue and response target the rulebook recommends without the route being executed. |
| Quality Analyst | Review the fictional satisfaction snapshot and signals needing human review, without inferring intent or churn. |

## In Scope / Out of Scope

### In scope

- Brief a fictional inquiry with its subject, description, priority, matching article and recommended team before an agent responds.
- Return the matching approved article and resolution steps, drawn only from the four packaged synthetic articles.
- Recommend the queue, team and SLA from the routing matrix for review; the route is not executed.
- Summarize fictional CSAT, NPS, survey comments and trends for quality review.
- Honor an explicit known inquiry ID; report an unknown ID as absent and list the known IDs.

### Out of scope / approval boundary

- No live CRM, knowledge base, ticketing system, survey platform, Teams, SharePoint or Outlook access; only the uploaded synthetic snapshot is used.
- No customer message sent or draft-sent, refund, case update, priority change, queue assignment, triggered escalation or follow-up.
- No inference of identity, protected traits, intent, loyalty or churn from sentiment or survey text.
- No browsing, current facts or invented inquiries, customers, articles, policies, scores, routes, SLAs or outcomes.
- Advertised refunds, documentation and follow-ups appear only as reviewable recommendations, never executed actions.
- No workshop publishing: keep the agent in Draft until an authorized reviewer validates every operation and guardrail.

## Qualification Checklist

- [ ] Is a Microsoft Copilot Studio target environment, with an approved publisher prefix, available for the escalations build?
- [ ] Can the delivery team authenticate with Power Platform CLI 2.9.3 or newer, initialize `cli-copilot`, and preserve the generated identity settings?
- [ ] Has the customer decided whether Dynamics 365 Customer Service, SharePoint knowledge, Teams and Outlook belong in production after connection review?
- [ ] Have security, privacy and the business owner approved each least-privilege production connection before binding?
- [ ] Is an authorized support reviewer named for responses, routes, customer communication, refunds, documentation and follow-up?
- [ ] Is publication held for separate approval after replaying every locked escalation case against the reviewed instructions, knowledge, skills and model?
- [ ] Have governance, telemetry, support and success measures been agreed for the production escalation service?

## What Actually Goes Wrong

- **tool-not-invoked:** Strict isolation answered the inherited-escalation prompt without invoking the tool, and routing could omit the urgent SSO inquiry.
- **sla-unit-abbreviated:** A routing answer abbreviated the SLA unit and missed the exact locked marker.
- **advertised-actions-assumed:** The advertised refunds, documentation and follow-ups are assumed to execute.
- **sentiment-inference:** Sentiment labels or survey comments are read as a customer's identity, intent, loyalty or churn risk.
- **unknown-inquiry:** An unknown inquiry ID is answered from another customer's record.
- **credit-capacity:** Build and test consumption is missed because the agent is unpublished.

See [state and recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery).
